teaching.hint: How many copies of one letter can fit around the available copies of the other?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Available opposite letters create gaps that can hold at most two copies of a repeated letter; a construction must preserve that remaining capacity.
solution_outline.approach: Build the string in short blocks. Favor the letter with the larger remaining count, but emit at most two copies before using an available opposite letter as a separator; alternate when counts are equal.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The remaining counts continue to satisfy the gap-capacity feasibility condition, and the current suffix never has a run longer than two.
solution_outline.correctness: The block choice reduces the larger remaining count while preserving the possibility of separating all future copies. Each block itself is valid and the separator prevents an invalid boundary run; termination uses exactly the requested counts.
solution_outline.complexity: O(a+b) time and O(a+b) output space; O(1) extra workspace.
solution_outline.pitfall: Appending the currently more frequent letter three times can create a forbidden run even if the final counts are feasible.

common_wrong_turns: Spend all copies of one letter first
Assume a count of zero always permits the other count arbitrarily large
source_fidelity_notes: Kept the guaranteed-existence condition and both zero-count edge cases; no sample output is prescribed.
